subject: Edo
examFormat: Two papers. Paper 1 is 60 multiple-choice items (Language 30, Literature 22, Culture 8) answered in 1 hour for 60 marks. Paper 2 is essay-type (Language, Literature and Culture), 2 hours for 100 marks: six questions in all (three from Section A, two from Section B, one from Section C), answered in Edo using the official orthography and metalanguage. Total 160 marks (Paper 1 30%, Paper 2 70%), scaled down to 100%.
excluded: Lists of selected texts for WASSCE 2014-2015 and 2016-2020 (set books change; described generically in the topics).

topics.name: Composition (Edo)
topics.content: Candidates are advised to write about 300 words and spend not more than 45 minutes on this section. The topic chosen will include any of the listed essay types: narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue, debate, letter writing.

topics.name: Sound System (Edo)
objectives: Explain the production of vowels, consonants and the syllabic nasal in terms of place and manner
Classify vowels, consonants and the syllabic nasal phonetically and phonemically
Explain sound processes such as vowel harmony, assimilation and elision
Describe the sound system aspect of the orthography
topics.content: Candidates answer one question from the two set in Paper 2.

topics.name: Grammar (Edo)
objectives: Explain word structure and word formation
Identify word classes: nouns, verbs, adverbs, pronouns, adjectives, etc.
Explain grammatical categories: subject, object, complement, predicate, number, person, tense, aspect, mood, etc.
Describe the structure and types of sentences
topics.content: Candidates answer one question from the two set in Paper 2.

topics.name: Oral Literature (Edo)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on oral prose, poetry and drama
topics.content: In Oral Literature there are three set books covering prose, poetry and drama; one question is set on each and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Written Literature (Edo)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on written prose, poetry and drama
topics.content: In Written Literature there are three set books covering prose, poetry and drama; one question is set on each and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Customs (Edo)
objectives: Describe home training: greetings, respect for superiors, cleanliness, tolerance, integrity, hard work, etc.
Describe funerals: traditional and modern methods
Describe inheritance: traditional and modern methods
topics.content: Section C: two questions are set and candidates answer one.

topics.name: Institutions (Edo)
objectives: Describe politics: family structure, age grades, chieftaincy, Obaship, etc.
Explain Edo beliefs about Osalobua/Osanobua (God), deities/divinities, other invisible forces, etc.
Describe modern religions: Islam, Christianity, etc.
Describe the economy: adverts, money lending, cooperative efforts, etc.
topics.content: Section C: two questions are set and candidates answer one.
